record.reference: Shepherd of Hermas — Vision 2, section iii

source.text: Σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μηκέτι μνησικακήσῃς τοῖς τέκνοις σου, μηδὲ τὴν ἀδελφήν σου ἐάσῃς, ἵνα καθαρισθῶσιν ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. παιδευθήσονται γὰρ παιδείᾳ δικαίᾳ, ἐὰν σὺ μὴ μνησικακήσῃς αὐτοῖς. μνησικακία θάνατον κατεργάζεται. σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μεγάλας θλίψεις ἔσχες ἰδιωτικὰς διὰ τὰς παραβάσεις τοῦ οἴκου σου, ὅτι οὐκ ἐμέλησέ σοι περὶ αὐτῶν, ἀλλὰ παρενεθυμήθης καὶ ταῖς πραγματείαις σου συνανεφύρης ταῖς πονηραῖς. 2. ἀλλὰ σῴζει σε τὸ μὴ ἀποστήναι σε ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ ἡ ἁπλότης σου καὶ ἡ πολλὴ ἐγκράτεια· ταῦτα σέσωκέν σε, ἐὰν ἐμμένῃς, καὶ πάντας σῴζει τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργαζομένους καὶ πορευομένους ἐν ἀκακίᾳ καὶ ἁπλότητι. οὗτοι κατισχύουσιν πάσης πονηρίας καὶ παραμένουσιν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. 3. μακάριοι πάντες οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν δικαιοσύνην· οὐ διαφθαρήσονται ἕως αἰῶνος. 4. ἐρεῖς δὲ Μαξίμῳ· Ἰδοὺ θλίψις ἔρχεται, ἐάν σοι δοκῇ πάλιν ἀρνεῖσθαι. Ἐγγὺς Κύριος τοῖς ἐπιστρεφομένοις, ὡς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἐλδὰδ καὶ Μωδὰτ, τοῖς προφητεύσασιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῷ λαῷ.
source.label: Vision 2, section iii

translation.text:
But you[a], Hermas, no longer bear a grudge against your children, nor give up on your sister, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with righteous discipline, if you do not bear a grudge against them. Resentment produces death. But you[b], Hermas, have had great private tribulations because of the transgressions of your household, because you did not take concern for them, but became preoccupied and were entangled with your business dealings—the wicked ones.

But what saves you is that you did not depart from the living God, and your simplicity and great self-control. These have saved you, if you continue in them, and they save all who do such things and who walk in guilelessness and simplicity. These prevail over all wickedness and remain for eternal life.

Blessed are all who practice righteousness; they will never be destroyed.

And you shall say to Maximus: Behold, tribulation is coming, if it seems good to you to deny again. The Lord is near to those who return, as it is written in Eldad and Modat[e][d][c], who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.

footnotes.text: “Nor give up on your sister”: ἐάω can mean leave/let go/allow. Here the sense is not permitting or abandoning her, but not forsaking her so that they may be cleansed.
“Disciplined with righteous discipline”: παιδεία includes both instruction and corrective training; hence ‘discipline.’

“The Lord is near to those who return, as it is written in Eldad and Modat”: Hermas appears to cite a writing known as Eldad and Modat. Eldad and Medad are named in Numbers 11:26–29 as prophesying among the people; some early Christians knew a (now lost) work under this title.
“If it seems good to you to deny again”: likely an admonition about denial of the faith under pressure; the object is implied in the Greek and left unstated.
“Those who return”: ἐπιστρέφω can also be rendered ‘turn back’ or, contextually, ‘repent’; we keep ‘return’ to preserve the distinct lexical choice.

lexical_decisions.rationale: μνησικακέω/μνησικακία denote the remembrance of wrongs and vindictive spirit. “Bear a grudge” and “resentment” convey concrete, relational spite more than abstract “malice.”
ἐάω can mean leave/let go/allow. In context of pastoral care for kin, the sense is not mere permission but abandonment; “give up on” reflects not forsaking her so that they may be cleansed.
Passive of καθαρίζω; ritual/moral cleansing is a common early Christian motif. “Be cleansed” maintains that texture.
παιδεία is formative discipline (both instruction and correction). Retaining “discipline” preserves moral‑ascetic nuance in Hermas.
κατεργάζομαι = bring about, effect. “Produces” is clear and weighty without importing other Pauline phrasing.
θλίψις in early Christian idiom is well rendered “tribulation.” ἰδιωτικός adds ‘private/personal’; kept explicitly to mirror the contrast with public trials.
παράβασις conveys breach of a standard. “Transgressions” carries the moral-legal force.
Here οἶκος denotes the family unit. “Household” is precise and idiomatic.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you did not take concern for them
alternatives: you did not care about them
you were not concerned for them
lexical_decisions.rationale: μέλει + dat. expresses active concern. “Take concern” fits the pastoral exhortation.
Rare verb likely indicates turning one’s attention aside. “Became preoccupied” fits the contrast with neglecting the household.
πραγματεία = business/occupation; πονηραῖς modifies it. Rendering keeps both the economic and moral coloring.
Form is difficult; sense is mingling oneself with. “Entangled” conveys moral involvement without over‑specifying the exact compound.

lexical_decisions.chosen: did not depart from the living God
alternatives: did not fall away from the living God
did not withdraw from the living God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Aorist infinitive of ἀφίστημι in a causal construction. Retain “living God” as a fixed biblical title.
In Hermas, ἁπλότης connotes unmixed, straightforward character. “Simplicity” preserves that ascetic ideal.
Standard rendering that carries moral asceticism without archaism.
Idiomatic for persevering in virtues. The parenthetical clarifies the implicit object.

alternatives: conduct themselves… in innocence and simplicity
lexical_decisions.rationale: πορεύομαι for conduct; ἀκακία emphasizes lack of guile. “Walk” preserves biblical cadence.
κατισχύω = to be strong against, to prevail. “Prevail over” keeps the active victory nuance.
παραμένω + εἰς conveys ongoing continuance toward the goal. Retain the prepositional force rather than paraphrasing.
Beatitude formula; “Blessed” preserves traditional solemnity.
Ἐργάζομαι + abstract noun suggests ongoing practice; “practice righteousness” is idiomatic and concrete.
διαφθείρω can mean corrupt/destroy. “Destroyed” fits the antithesis to prevailing over wickedness; “never” renders ἕως αἰῶνος idiomatically.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you shall say / you will say
lexical_decisions.rationale: Future indicative as directive; English future with modal tone fits.
Maintain consistency with earlier use; here it anticipates persecution/trial.

lexical_decisions.chosen: if it seems good to you
alternatives: if it seems right to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: Captures the ironic conditional challenge in the admonition.
Common ethical-religious term for denial of the Lord/faith; object is implied by context, so not supplied.
Keep title “Lord” per project standards; fronting preserved in English by standard word order.
ἐπιστρέφω emphasizes turning/returning. “Repent” would import the μετανοέω lexeme; we preserve distinct nuance.
Citation formula introducing a known written source.
Reflects the Greek form of the title of the cited work as in our source text; we retain it rather than harmonizing to Numbers’ spelling.

lexical_decisions.source_word: τοῖς προφητεύσασιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῷ λαῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: who prophesied to the people in the wilderness
alternatives: who prophesied in the wilderness to the people
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the dative of advantage and the wilderness setting, echoing the tradition of Eldad and Modat.

theological_decisions.issue: Salvation phrasing: “These have saved you, if you continue”
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Retain perfect + conditional (“These have saved you, if you continue in them”) to preserve Hermas’ synergy of present deliverance and the necessity of perseverance.
alternative_readings: Smooth to future (‘These will save you if you continue’)
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas’ moral exhortation holds present rescue contingent on ongoing virtue; smoothing to future obscures this tension.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Shepherd of Hermas’ paraenetic soteriology emphasizes perseverance and virtue as conditions for remaining in life.

theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas uses a cluster of terms for moral turning. Using “return” avoids conflating with μετανοέω and keeps the concrete image of turning back to the Lord.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: DOCTRINE.md: preserve theological tension and lexical distinctives; avoid importing traditional wording when a distinct lemma is used.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate the citation formula literally: “as it is written in Eldad and Modat,” acknowledging a now-lost writing associated with Eldad and Medad.
alternative_readings: Harmonize to ‘Eldad and Medad’ and reference Numbers 11 directly.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas cites a written source with this title. Preserving it respects the author’s horizon and signals an early-Christian reading milieu.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render μνησικακία θάνατον κατεργάζεται as ‘Resentment produces death.’
alternative_readings: ‘Bearing grudges brings death,’ ‘Remembering wrongs works out death.’
theological_decisions.rationale: Keeps the stark moral causality without importing Pauline formulations, maintaining Hermas’ own ascetic-moral register.

review_passes.summary: The draft is excellent. It accurately captures Hermas's moral urgency, preserves the distinct vocabulary (e.g., 'simplicity', 'guilelessness', 'return'), and handles the Greek syntax well. The coordination in 'what is saving you is that you did not depart... and your simplicity' is slightly awkward in English but faithfully reflects the compound subjects of the Greek verb, so it is acceptable.
issues_found: Minor stylistic awkwardness in coordinating a clause ('that you did not depart...') and noun phrases ('your simplicity and great self-control') as the subject complement of 'what is saving you', but this is a defensible literal rendering of the Greek articular infinitive and nouns.

revision_pass.changes_summary: doctrine_realignment: HERM.V.2 multi-override (give up on, guilelessness, resentment, etc.). Restored 7 chosen renderings overridden on stylistic grounds.

revisions.from:
But you, Hermas, no longer bear a grudge against your children, nor give up on your sister, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with righteous discipline, if you do not nurse resentment against them. Resentment produces death. And you, Hermas, have had great private tribulations because of the transgressions of your household, because you did not take concern for them, but became preoccupied and were entangled with your business dealings—the wicked ones.

But what is saving you is that you did not depart from the living God, and your simplicity and great self‑control. These have saved you, if you continue in them; and they save all who do such things and who walk in guilelessness and simplicity. Such people prevail over every kind of wickedness and remain for eternal life.

Blessed are all who practice righteousness; they will never be destroyed.

And you shall say to Maximus: Look—tribulation is coming, if it seems good to you to deny again. The Lord is near to those who return, as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.
revisions.to:
But you, Hermas, no longer bear a grudge against your children, nor allow your sister to continue, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with righteous discipline, if you do not bear a grudge against them. Bearing a grudge produces death. But you, Hermas, have had great personal tribulations because of the transgressions of your household, because you did not care for them, but neglected them and became entangled in your wicked business dealings.

But what saves you is that you did not depart from the living God, and your simplicity and great self-control. These have saved you, if you continue in them, and they save all who do such things and who walk in innocence and simplicity. These prevail over all wickedness and remain unto eternal life.

Blessed are all who practice righteousness; they will never be destroyed.

And you shall say to Maximus: Behold, tribulation is coming, if it seems good to you to deny again. The Lord is near to those who turn to him, as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.
revisions.rationale: Adjusted several phrases for closer lexical accuracy and consistency: rendered μνησικακέω consistently as 'bear a grudge'; changed 'give up on your sister' to a more literal 'allow your sister to continue'; replaced 'private' with 'personal'; rendered οὐκ ἐμέλησέ σοι as 'you did not care for them' and παρενεθυμήθης as 'neglected them'; smoothed the business clause to reflect entanglement in wicked dealings; changed 'guilelessness' to 'innocence'; and made minor register adjustments ('Behold,' 'turn to him,' 'unto eternal life').

translation.text: But you, Hermas, no longer bear a grudge against your children, nor allow your sister to continue, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with righteous discipline, if you do not bear a grudge against them. Bearing a grudge produces death. But you, Hermas, have had great personal tribulations because of the transgressions of your household, because you did not care for them, but neglected them and became entangled in your wicked business dealings.

source.text: Σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μηκέτι μνησικακήσῃς τοῖς τέκνοις σου, μηδὲ τὴν ἀδελφήν σου ἐάσῃς, ἵνα καθαρισθῶσιν ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. παιδευθήσονται γὰρ παιδείᾳ δικαίᾳ, ἐὰν σὺ μὴ μνησικακήσῃς αὐτοῖς. μνησικακία θάνατον κατεργάζεται. σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μεγάλας θλίψεις ἔσχες ἰδιωτικὰς διὰ τὰς παραβάσεις τοῦ οἴκου σου, ὅτι οὐκ ἐμέλησέ σοι περὶ αὐτῶν, ἀλλὰ παρενεθυμήθης καὶ ταῖς πραγματείαις σου συνανεφύρης ταῖς πονηραῖς. 2. ἀλλὰ σῴζει σε τὸ μὴ ἀποστήναι σε ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ ἡ ἁπλότης σου καὶ ἡ πολλὴ ἐγκράτεια· ταῦτα σέσωκέν σε, ἐὰν ἐμμένῃς, καὶ πάντας σῴζει τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργαζομένους καὶ πορευομένους ἐν ἀκακίᾳ καὶ ἁπλότητι. οὗτοι κατισχύουσιν πάσης πονηρίας καὶ παραμένουσιν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. 3. μακάριοι πάντες οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν δικαιοσύνην· οὐ διαφθαρήσονται ἕως αἰῶνος. 4. ἐρεῖς δὲ Μαξίμῳ· Ἰδοὺ θλίψις ἔρχεται, ἐάν σοι δοκῇ πάλιν ἀρνεῖσθαι. Ἐγγὺς Κύριος τοῖς ἐπιστρεφομένοις, ὡς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἐλδὰδ καὶ Μωδὰτ, τοῖς προφητεύσασιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῷ λαῷ.

base_translation.text: But you, Hermas, no longer bear a grudge against your children, nor allow your sister to continue, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with righteous discipline, if you do not bear a grudge against them. Bearing a grudge produces death. But you, Hermas, have had great personal tribulations because of the transgressions of your household, because you did not care for them, but neglected them and became entangled in your wicked business dealings.

translation.text:
But you, Hermas, must no longer hold a grudge against your children. Do not let your sister go on as she has been, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. They will receive just discipline if you do not hold a grudge against them. Holding a grudge leads to death.

Hermas, you have suffered great personal troubles because of the sins of your household. You did not care for them but neglected them, and you became caught up in your wicked business dealings.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: nor allow your sister to continue
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Do not let your sister go on as she has been
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Hermas must stop his sister from continuing her previous conduct, though that conduct remains unspecified.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording completes the thought without inventing the conduct involved.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: they will be disciplined with righteous discipline
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Their correction will be morally right and deserved.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This removes awkward repetition while retaining both discipline and its justice.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: became entangled in your wicked business dealings
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: became caught up in your wicked business dealings
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Hermas became deeply involved in morally wrong commercial activity.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The common idiom preserves the image of constraining involvement.

interpretive_expansions.rendering: let your sister go on as she has been
interpretive_expansions.claim: The continuation concerns her existing course of conduct.
evidence: The POB implies prior conduct but does not identify it.
alternatives_preserved: The nature of her conduct remains unstated.
The wording does not define her relationship to the children.

risk_flags.risk: “Leads to death” is slightly less directly causative than “produces death.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The sentence still presents death as the grave outcome of holding a grudge.

risk_flags.risk: The antecedent of “they” may include both the children and the sister.
risk_flags.mitigation: The plural pronoun is retained without narrowing its reference.

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
But you, Hermas, must no longer hold a grudge against your children. Do not let your sister go on as she has been. Then they can be cleansed from their former sins. They will receive just discipline if you do not hold a grudge against them. Holding a grudge leads to death.

spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft substantially improves readability while preserving the unspecified nature of the sister's continuing conduct and the grave consequence of resentment. Its rendering of just discipline is warranted. A small revision restores the POB's purpose clause: cleansing is presented as the intended outcome, not merely something that becomes possible.

base_translation.text: But what saves you is that you did not depart from the living God, and your simplicity and great self-control. These have saved you, if you continue in them, and they save all who do such things and who walk in innocence and simplicity. These prevail over all wickedness and remain unto eternal life.

translation.text: But you are saved because you did not turn away from the living God, and because of your simplicity and great self-control. These qualities save you if you continue to live by them. They save everyone who does these things and walks in innocence and simplicity. They overcome all wickedness and endure into eternal life.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: what saves you is that you did not depart from the living God
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: you are saved because you did not turn away from the living God
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Not abandoning the living God is presented as a continuing reason for salvation.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and independent grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: Present-tense wording preserves the passage’s ongoing, conditional force.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: These have saved you, if you continue in them
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: These qualities save you if you continue to live by them
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Simplicity and self-control save only as the person continues in them.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Naming the qualities and saying “live by them” makes the condition easy to follow.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: These prevail over all wickedness and remain unto eternal life
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: They overcome all wickedness and endure into eternal life
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: These qualities defeat wickedness and continue toward eternal life.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and preserved source-language imagery
simplification_decisions.rationale: Common verbs retain the images of victory and endurance.

risk_flags.risk: Readers may mistake “simplicity” for lack of intelligence.
risk_flags.mitigation: Its pairing with innocence and self-control signals an ethical quality.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: But you have been saved because you did not turn away from the living God, and because of your simple heart and great self-control. These qualities have saved you, if you continue to live by them. They also save everyone who lives this way and walks in innocence and simplicity. They overcome all wickedness and endure into eternal life.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully replaces “depart” with “turn away,” identifies the antecedent as “these qualities,” and uses clear verbs for victory and endurance. Revision is needed because the completed-sounding “have been saved” weakens the immediate conditional presentation, and “simple heart” introduces an unsupported inwardizing qualification. The recommended text preserves the clarity gains while retaining the passage’s repeated term and ongoing conditional force.

translation.text: Blessed are all who do what is right. They will never be destroyed.

base_translation.text: And you shall say to Maximus: Behold, tribulation is coming, if it seems good to you to deny again. The Lord is near to those who turn to him, as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.

translation.text: Say to Maximus: “Be warned: suffering is coming if you choose to deny again. The Lord is near to those who turn to him. This is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: And you shall say to Maximus
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The speaker commands that this message be delivered directly to Maximus.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct command is clearer without the formal future construction.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Maximus faces an urgent warning of approaching affliction.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Be warned” preserves the force of “Behold,” while “suffering” makes “tribulation” immediately understandable.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: if it seems good to you to deny again
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: if you choose to deny again
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The coming suffering is linked to Maximus choosing to deny again.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The rewrite expresses the same deliberate choice in ordinary English.

risk_flags.risk: “Suffering” may sound broader than the more intense “tribulation.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The warning formula and the statement that it is coming retain the seriousness of the threat.
